title: 'Mega Masters' Hearings Pack Immigration Courts as Administration Pushes to Accelerate Deportations
excerpt: Immigration courts are scheduling hearings with 100 or more people at once — up from the typical two or three dozen — in a strategy experts say is designed to maximize removal orders.
body:
• Immigration courts are scheduling 'mega masters' hearings with 100 or more respondents at once, up from the typical 20-30, to speed up deportation orders.
  • The Trump administration has also proposed tripling fees for immigration court filings — an appeal would jump from $110 to $975 — potentially deterring immigrants from contesting removal.
  • Immigration attorneys say the hearings disproportionately target unrepresented immigrants, with those who arrive late or miss court automatically receiving removal orders.
  • Courts have already issued over 4,000 removal orders in Michigan alone since October 2025, on pace for the most in three decades.

Immigration courts across the United States are deploying an unprecedented strategy to accelerate deportation proceedings: scheduling massive master calendar hearings that pack more than 100 respondents into a single session, according to immigration attorneys and the American Immigration Lawyers Association.

The tactic, dubbed "mega masters" by practitioners, represents a sharp departure from the typical master calendar hearing, which previously included two to three dozen people. For many immigrants, this initial appearance is their first and sometimes only chance to make their case to remain in the country.

How Mega Masters Work

The hearings have been documented in immigration courts in Chicago, Boston, Chelmsford, Massachusetts, and Dallas, with attorneys warning the practice is spreading to additional jurisdictions. The strategy largely targets immigrants without legal representation — those most vulnerable to procedural missteps that result in automatic deportation orders.

https://x.com/RealAmVoice/status/2080678268349349989

"The major concern is that this is going to be a group of people without attorneys, that they're not going to have gotten proper notice," said Vanessa Dojaquez-Torres, practicing policy counsel at AILA. She added that courts often lack enough seats for hearings with so many people, making it "almost like they are being designed to increase" the number of automatic deportation orders.

Those who show up late or fail to appear receive in absentia removal orders, further truncating the already limited due process available in immigration proceedings.

"Children are now facing the real possibility of representing themselves in court alone, against experienced government attorneys."

— Heidi Devereaux, Michigan Immigrant Rights Center

Fee Hikes Add Another Barrier

Compounding the pressure, the Trump administration this week proposed a rule that would triple some immigration court filing fees. Under the proposal from the Justice Department's Executive Office for Immigration Review, the cost to appeal an immigration judge's decision would leap from $110 to $975. Forms for cancellation of removal would jump from $100 to over $300.

While fee waivers may be available in some cases, immigration advocates warn that the increases would effectively price many immigrants out of contesting their deportation orders — particularly those already struggling to find legal representation.

The Numbers Tell the Story

From October 2025 to June 2026, judges in the Detroit Immigration Court alone ordered more than 4,000 people deported, according to the Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse at Syracuse University. That pace would make it the most removal orders from Michigan's only immigration court in at least three decades.

The acceleration is part of President Trump's stated goal of deporting one million people per year, roughly double the 600,000 removed in 2025. Trump has publicly complained about the backlog of millions of cases in immigration courts, framing the courts as an obstacle to rapid deportation rather than a venue for due process.

Impact on the Indian Community

While the mega masters strategy primarily targets undocumented immigrants from Latin America, the broader shifts in immigration court procedure affect all immigrants in removal proceedings — including Indian nationals who may face deportation after visa overstays or application denials. The proposed fee increases would also affect anyone filing motions or appeals in immigration court, regardless of nationality.

With the immigration court system under mounting pressure to process cases faster and with fewer procedural safeguards, immigration attorneys are urging anyone facing proceedings to secure legal representation as early as possible.
